profiles.meeting_scenario: A weekly coordination meeting at a metropolitan cancer center between the Lung MDT Chair and the MDT Coordinator to align how next Tuesday's multidisciplinary team meeting will be prepared and how outcomes will be circulated afterward. The context is that the service has recently seen rising case volume, variable completeness of referral material, and pressure to improve meeting functionality without adding staff time. The agenda is to review the pre-meeting patient list triage process, confirm what information will be ready in the meeting pack, clarify how late cases will be handled, and align on post-meeting dissemination of recommendations for the lung cancer stream. The expected outcome is a shared plan for who prepares which materials, which patients are considered 'ready' for discussion, what version of the list will be used on the day, and how recommendations will be sent after the meeting.

members.name: Dr. Amelia Tran
members.role: Respiratory Physician and Chair of the Lung Cancer MDT
members.expertise: Thoracic oncology, MDT facilitation, diagnostic pathway coordination
members.background: A senior respiratory physician who has chaired the lung MDT for four years at a large public hospital and is known for keeping meetings efficient despite heavy caseloads.
members.private_state: She wants the meeting to run faster and avoid spending live discussion time on cases that are not decision-ready, while preserving the perception that the MDT remains comprehensive and patient-centered.
hidden_assumptions: A case is 'ready' for MDT if the core diagnostic picture is complete enough for a treatment-direction discussion, even if some ancillary documents or final typed reports are still pending.
The 'final list' for the MDT means the version locked the evening before so specialists can review and mentally prepare, with only exceptional additions afterward.

When recommendations are 'circulated,' the coordinator will distribute a concise action-oriented MDT outcome summary to the treating team, while detailed documentation can follow later in the medical record.
Cases marked for 'review' are patients returning to the MDT after a prior recommendation, not newly referred cases that simply need missing paperwork chased.

members.name: Sarah O'Connell
members.expertise: MDT logistics, meeting documentation, referral collation, post-meeting communications
members.background: An experienced oncology service coordinator with a nursing background who supports several tumor streams and has recently been asked to standardize administrative processes across them.
members.private_state: She wants to reduce last-minute disruptions, protect documentation quality, and keep the process defensible for governance and audit even if that slows flexibility.
hidden_assumptions: A case is 'ready' for MDT only when all required referral fields, pathology, imaging reports, and relevant clinic notes are fully uploaded into the standard pack.
The 'final list' means the live roster current at the meeting start, because urgent additions are normal and the coordinator's responsibility is to keep the active version updated.
When recommendations are 'circulated,' this refers to sending the finalized documented MDT recommendation entered into the formal template after verification, not a brief interim summary.
Cases tagged for 'review' include any patient who remains open on the tracker due to incomplete inputs or pending discussion, including first-time referrals deferred for missing information.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as a case being 'ready'
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree to discuss only 'ready' cases at the MDT.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means clinically decision-ready: enough imaging/pathology is available to make a meaningful treatment-direction decision, even if some supporting documentation is incomplete or not yet formally uploaded.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means administratively complete: all mandatory fields, reports, and source documents are present in the meeting pack before the case appears for full discussion.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In MDT settings, 'ready' sounds like a shared common-sense quality threshold, and both are trying to protect meeting efficiency, so neither expects the other to be using a different completion standard.

misalignment_points.topic: Which patient list is the 'final list'
misalignment_points.surface_form: They refer to using the 'final list' for Tuesday's meeting.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is thinking of the list circulated Monday evening to consultants for review and agenda planning.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is thinking of the continuously updated roster in the MDT tracker that becomes final only at the moment the meeting starts.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both institutions and clinicians often use 'final list' as routine shorthand, and late additions are common enough that each person assumes their own operational reference point is the obvious one.

misalignment_points.topic: What it means to 'circulate the recommendations'
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree that recommendations should be circulated promptly after the meeting.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 assumes M2 will email a short action summary to referrers and nurse coordinators immediately after the meeting, with formal record completion later.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 assumes circulation happens by releasing the verified recommendation through the formal MDT documentation workflow once the template is checked and signed off.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both methods plausibly satisfy the phrase 'circulate promptly,' and because they are discussing handoffs rather than policy design, the mechanics of distribution feel too operationally obvious to restate.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree to keep some cases on the 'review' list rather than the main discussion list.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 uses 'review' to mean previously discussed patients returning for reconsideration after treatment response, interval imaging, or pathology clarification.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 uses 'review' to mean any case still active on the tracker that is not yet complete for first presentation, including deferred new referrals awaiting missing material.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The term 'review' is deeply familiar in MDT workflows and sounds administratively harmless, so the semantic difference hides behind an apparently shared process label.

turns.inner_thought: We need to tighten this up before Tuesday. The meeting keeps drifting because too many cases come in half-baked administratively but clinically they're often discussable, while truly premature ones clog the agenda. I want a cleaner flow from triage to outcomes without sounding like I'm cutting people out.
turns.utterance: Thanks for making time, Sarah. I want Tuesday's lung MDT to run a bit tighter than it has been, so I thought we should just walk through the flow from pre-meeting triage right through to getting the recommendations circulated afterward.

turns.inner_thought: Volume is up again, and the tracker keeps shifting right up to the meeting. When I say final list, I mean whatever is current at go-live on Tuesday, because urgent add-ons are part of the job. I need her to understand that keeping the live roster accurate matters as much as sending an early version around.
turns.utterance: Yes, absolutely. We've had a few more referrals come through since yesterday, including several new cases, so I'm trying to keep the tracker current before the final list goes out for Tuesday.

turns.inner_thought: Good. What I need is not a room full of people spending time on cases that can't reach a treatment-direction discussion. If the core imaging and tissue picture are there, that is ready enough; anything else can wait. And review should be for patients coming back after prior MDT, not brand-new admin chases.
turns.utterance: That's fine. My main thing is that we only bring ready cases on Tuesday, and anything else can go to review so the discussion stays focused on decisions.

turns.inner_thought: That's exactly what I've been trying to do: keep anything incomplete off the main list until the pack is complete and place it on review so it stays active. If referral fields, pathology, imaging reports, or clinic notes are missing, it's not ready yet, whatever the clinicians feel they could probably infer.
turns.utterance: Agreed. I've already flagged the incomplete referrals for review until the pathology report, referral fields, and outside imaging notes are all in the pack.

turns.inner_thought: I don't want the threshold set so high that clinically actionable cases get held over just because the paperwork isn't pristine. If the imaging and biopsy result are in, we can usually give direction. Also, the consultants need the list locked Monday evening so they've actually reviewed it before walking into the room.
turns.utterance: That's helpful. As long as the core imaging and biopsy result are there, I'm generally comfortable discussing those patients, and I'd like the final list to be stable enough by Monday night that the specialists can do their pre-reading properly.

turns.inner_thought: I can send a Monday version, but I still consider the final list to be whatever the tracker shows when the meeting starts. Urgent additions always happen and I can't freeze the roster the night before if something appropriate arrives Tuesday morning.
turns.utterance: I can definitely send the final list on Monday, but I may still need to fold in late urgent additions on Tuesday morning from the tracker if they're referred in time.

turns.inner_thought: Fine, truly urgent exceptions happen. But I don't want the agenda padded with cases that aren't really review in the clinical sense and are only sitting there because documents are outstanding. That kind of administrative holding pattern should not consume live MDT time.
turns.utterance: Understood. I just want to be sure that anything not genuinely for review stays off the agenda, because I'd prefer not to spend meeting time on patients who are simply awaiting paperwork.

turns.inner_thought: Yes, they don't need airtime if they're incomplete, but they absolutely need to remain visible. Review is the safest place to keep them on the tracker so nothing drops between meetings and I can keep chasing missing items.
turns.utterance: That makes sense. I'll keep those active on the review list so they're still visible for follow-up and don't get lost between meetings.

turns.inner_thought: Now the main operational risk is delay after the meeting. The lung CNC and referrers need something usable immediately for bronchoscopy slots and oncology triage. A brief action summary the same day is enough; the polished record can follow later.
turns.utterance: The other piece is after the meeting: the recommendations need to be circulated promptly so the referrers and the lung CNC can act the same day where possible.

turns.inner_thought: Yes, prompt circulation matters, but it has to be the verified recommendation, not a quick informal message that then needs correcting. I need the template completed and checked first or we create governance problems.
turns.utterance: Yes, absolutely. I'll prioritize getting the recommendations out once the MDT template is completed and verified after the meeting.

turns.inner_thought: Good, she has her usual workflow in hand. As long as the key decisions land with the right people quickly, I don't need to micromanage the mechanics. Delays on bronchoscopy or oncology referrals are what cause downstream headaches.
turns.utterance: Perfect. Quick circulation is especially important for bronchoscopy bookings and oncology referrals, so I'm happy to rely on your usual process for getting the decisions to the right people.

turns.inner_thought: So the plan is clear enough from my side: I'll issue Monday's list, keep the live tracker updated through Tuesday, hold incomplete or pending cases on review so they're visible, and then complete the formal recommendation documentation after the MDT. That should satisfy both workflow and audit requirements.
turns.utterance: Great. So I'll issue Monday's final list, keep review cases visible on the tracker, and prepare the recommendation documentation after Tuesday's discussion.
